unigetui.changelog:
# Devolutions UniGetUI 2026.3.4

This release adds a docked package details panel, a Manager Health page, and two new extensions: Agent Skills, and Xcode on macOS. It also adds new options for updates, notifications and shutting down, and fixes many update, display and performance bugs.

### New Features
* Added a package details panel that can stay open beside the package list on the Installed, Discover and Updates pages. It follows the selected package. Open it from the footer, with Ctrl+Shift+D (Cmd+Shift+I on macOS), or from the right-click menu.
* Added a Manager Health page that shows when each package manager last worked or failed, with repair actions. Each package manager also has a setup guide, linked from its status card when the tool isn't found.
* Added an Agent Skills extension for finding, installing and updating skills and plugins for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot and Cursor. It is off by default, under Settings > Extensions.
* Added an Xcode extension on macOS 13 and later. It downloads, installs, updates and switches between several Xcode versions, and manages Simulator runtimes, after you sign in with your Apple ID. It is off by default, under Settings > Extensions.
* Git Repositories now shows the size of each clone and worktree, and handles refresh failures more clearly.
* When a UniGetUI update is ready, you can now read its release notes before installing it, then update now, update when you quit, or skip that version. Open it from the update notification or from **More > Check for UniGetUI updates**. Quitting UniGetUI no longer installs a waiting update unless you choose to.
* Added an option to install UniGetUI updates automatically while it runs in the background with nothing else in progress (Windows, off by default).
* New per-package installation options:
  * **Skip major updates**, to keep getting minor and patch releases without moving to the next major version.
  * **Uninstall, then reinstall when updated**, for packages that only update cleanly from scratch.
* Added **Shut down when finished** to the operations panel menu (Windows). It shuts the computer down after the current operations, with a 60-second countdown you can cancel.
* Added an option to quit UniGetUI when automatic updates find nothing to install.
* Added an option to keep update notifications on screen until you dismiss them (Windows).
* Package lists can now scroll horizontally instead of squeezing columns. Turn off **Fit columns to the window** in the column menu.

### Improvements
* Downloaded installers are now checked against their published hash, and the installer's signer is shown.
* .NET Tool now uses the feeds in your NuGet configuration, including private feeds, and detects updates on Artifactory feeds.
* Improvements to WinGet searches.
* WinGet now lists updates that it can only apply by reinstalling, for example when a new version switches installer type.
* At startup, update checks now wait for each package manager's installed list, which reduces the load on machines with many packages.
* Pip no longer uses or updates Python environments that belong to other apps.
* Grid and icon cards on Software Updates now show the new version.
* Indeterminate progress bars use much less GPU on Windows.
* Screen readers now announce the tab names in installation options and operation history.

### Bug Fixes
* Fixed a restart staying pending forever after rebooting.
* Fixed WinGet offering an update when another installed copy of the app was already newer.
* Fixed Steam and other launcher games being listed as WinGet packages with a permanent update.
* Fixed WinGet portable apps losing their command links when updated without administrator rights.
* Fixed an empty Discover search returning nothing on some private WinGet repositories.
* Fixed the installer-host warning showing again on every update of some packages.
* Fixed scheduled update checks installing updates at startup.
* Fixed the operation history file growing to hundreds of MB and using gigabytes of memory.
* Fixed UniGetUI repeatedly offering a self-update it couldn't install on Linux `.deb` and `.rpm` installs.
* Fixed the window frame, shadow and corners when Windows 11's rounded corners are turned off, and centered the Close button.

Thank you to everyone who reported issues and contributed improvements to the project.

**Full Changelog:** https://github.com/Devolutions/UniGetUI/compare/v2026.3.3...v2026.3.4

mpv.changelog:
We are excited to announce the release of mpv 0.42.0.

Key highlights:

* libcurl based network backend with HTTP/2, HTTP/3 and connection reuse
* DVD-Video, Blu-ray HDMV and BD-J menu navigation
* DVD-Audio playback
* Direct playback of .iso images of DVD-Video, DVD-Audio and Blu-ray discs
* Dolby Vision Profile 7 enhancement layer support in `gpu-next`
* MPEG-TS programs and HLS variants are exposed as editions
* DSD-over-PCM (DoP) passthrough with `--audio-spdif=dsd`
* Support for SRV3 (YouTube) subtitles via subrandr library
* Context menu populated from the new `menu.conf`, bound to right click
* `floating` OSC layout with Fluent icons (`--script-opts=osc-layout=floating`)
* API that allows integration between the OSC and (third-party) thumbnailer scripts
* Wayland session management
* Wayland color management through the protocol instead of the Vulkan API
* scRGB output with `--target-trc=scrgb`
* Improved HDR colorspace signalling on DRM (Linux)
* D3D11 render API backend for libmpv
* Reworked terminal video outputs (`sixel`, `kitty` and `tct`)
* AMD Frame Rate Conversion filter (`--vf=amf_frc`)
* Rewritten display-sync audio drift compensation
* `--tls-verify` is enabled by default

This release requires FFmpeg 6.1 or newer and libplacebo 7.387.0 or newer.

Note that the release binary assets are our [CI builds](https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/actions/runs/41936479105). These builds are reasonably useful. The Windows _full_ builds (`*-w64-mingw32-full.zip`) are bigger and aim to provide the complete experience.

trilium.changelog:
# v0.107.0
> [!NOTE]
> If you enjoyed this release, consider showing a token of appreciation by:
> 
> *   Pressing the “Star” button on [GitHub](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium) (top-right).
> *   Considering a one-time or recurrent donation to the [lead developer](https://github.com/eliandoran) via [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/eliandoran) or [PayPal](https://paypal.me/eliandoran).

> [!TIP]
> For Linux users: Trilium is now available on [Flathub](https://flathub.org/en/apps/org.triliumnotes.Trilium)!

This is the release where a text note stops being a single document. Notes can be embedded, quoted and referenced inside other notes and edited where they appear, laid out in columns and tabs, and mixed with drawings, attached files and video. Tables in text notes get the tools they had been missing, from merged cells to sorting, and the old layout is gone, a year after the new one replaced it.

Around the editor, the parts of the app that everyone touches were rebuilt: the context menus and the note autocomplete, the full search and the jump dialog, the launch bar and the tree. Shared pages look like the app again and render collections with their own views, and the calendar and geo map collections get the properties dialogs the board already had.

The AI integration becomes something to trust with a real database: every tool call asks before it reads or changes a note, a ChatGPT Codex subscription can stand in for an API key, and local models get web search through a search engine of your choice. On phones, iOS has a new layout and both apps navigate without a sidebar.

## 💡 Key highlights

### The text editor became a block editor

A text note used to be a document: one body of rich text, with other notes reachable only through links. It is now a composition. A note can embed another note and let you edit it where it sits, quote a few of its blocks and keep the quote current, or point at one paragraph of it instead of at the whole note.

*   [Editable transclusion](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11926): an included text or code note is edited inside the host note with the full editor, and one undo history covers both.
*   [Live excerpts](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11925) quote blocks of another note. They stay in sync, and an edit made in the excerpt is saved back to the source.
*   [Block references](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/12069) link to a paragraph, heading, table or range of blocks. The target opens scrolled to the block and highlighted, and on a shared page every block has a public link of its own.

Layout caught up with content. [Multicolumn layouts](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11958) put two to four columns side by side and stack them on narrow screens. [Drawing canvases](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11829) are sketched in place with Excalidraw and saved with the note. Files are [attached](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11795) in one step, as inline embeds for PDFs and spreadsheets or as links, and YouTube videos and web audio or video play inside the note. A block handle moves blocks, images and tables, a "+" on an empty line opens the slash commands, and one [link dialog](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/12358) serves web links, note links and anchors from a popover at the cursor.

The include box itself was [reworked](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11798): a compact title row with a caption, fullscreen, a link from the embed to its note and back, Markdown included as source, split or preview, code with folding and line numbers, and resizing by dragging a corner or an edge.

Contributed by @adoriandoran.

### Tables in text notes

Tables were the editor's weak spot: no merged cells, no sorting, and anything past a few rows meant switching to a spreadsheet note. The [table context menu](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11774) now merges and unmerges cells, distributes columns, and inserts or deletes many rows and columns at once. A column sorts by its values, with dates, times, numbers and text detected and ordered per the note's language, and Alt+arrows move rows and columns while keeping merged cells and header rows intact.

Wide tables scroll sideways under a sticky header, and on touch screens a column bar resizes and selects columns while corner handles select cell ranges. The insert form takes any size up to 1000 × 100, with header rows and columns.

Contributed by @adoriandoran.

### AI that asks before it acts

Two things kept many users away from the AI integration: paying per token, and handing a model write access to their notes. Both change in this release.

ChatGPT Codex subscriptions, including the free plan, and OpenRouter join Claude Code, GitHub Copilot and Antigravity as providers, so an existing subscription can drive Trilium's chat. [Custom search engines](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11878) (Brave Search, Tavily, Exa, Serper, Perplexity, or a self-hosted SearXNG) give web search to local models and to providers that have none of their own, such as DeepSeek.

[Before a tool runs](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/12116), the chat shows what the AI is about to read or change and waits for you to allow or deny it, for that call or for the rest of the conversation. The Tools menu sets the default: always ask, ask only before changes, or never ask. It works the same with API keys and with subscription providers.

### Shared pages look like the app

A note shared to the web rendered in a theme of its own, and a shared collection appeared as a plain list of its children. Shared pages now use a [theme built from the app's own look](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11979), in light and dark, and a shared board, table, calendar or other collection renders with the same view it has inside Trilium.

Drawings appear as theme-aware SVG pictures instead of a download link, and every bloc

Verified against the packaged, signed macOS build. Windows and Linux packages were verified from the produced release artifacts, their sizes and update manifests, rather than by running them.

Base checks

- Launch, open a file passed on the command line, add and edit shapes, change styles, undo and redo, copy and paste, save and reopen, insert, rename and delete pages, and zoom

restic.changelog:
Changelog for restic 0.19.1 (2026-07-05)
=======================================

The following sections list the changes in restic 0.19.1 relevant to restic users. The changes are ordered by importance.

Summary
-------

 * Fix [#5234](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5234): Prevent mounting over the repository directory
 * Fix [#5667](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5667): Skip inaccessible `backup` source paths
 * Fix [#5722](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5722): Update `mount` latest symlink after snapshot reload
 * Fix [#21866](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21866): Hide `stats` progress bar in JSON mode
 * Fix [#21869](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21869): Restore old behavior of `snapshots --latest <n>` without `--group-by`
 * Fix [#21876](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21876): Show timezone location in `snapshots` output
 * Fix [#21879](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21879): Prevent crash in mountpoint validation if mountpoint is inaccessible
 * Fix [#21895](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21895): Remove read-only files via the SFTP backend on Windows servers
 * Fix [#21899](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21899): Make `backup` respect excludes for duplicate directory entries

Details
-------

 * Bugfix #5234: Prevent mounting over the repository directory

   Using a local repository directory as the `mount` target — or a path that contains it, or that it contains — caused the FUSE server to read its own backend files through the new mount, deadlocking the kernel and requiring a long reboot to recover.

   Restic now resolves both paths and refuses any such overlap with a clear error before mounting.

    [#5234](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5234) [#5348](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/5348) 

 * Bugfix #5667: Skip inaccessible `backup` source paths

   The `backup` command only skipped source paths that did not exist. A path that could not be accessed for another reason, such as a malformed path on Windows, was kept and produced an empty snapshot. Restic now skips any such path and aborts if none remain.

    [#5667](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5667) [#21852](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21852) 

 * Bugfix #5722: Update `mount` latest symlink after snapshot reload

   When `restic mount` was kept running while new snapshots were created, the new snapshots appeared in the mountpoint, but the `latest` symlink could still point to the previously latest snapshot. Restic now invalidates the cached snapshot directory entries after a snapshot reload so that `latest` points to the newest snapshot.

    [#5722](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5722) [#21873](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21873) 

 * Bugfix #21866: Hide `stats` progress bar in JSON mode

   Since restic 0.19.0, the `stats` command shows a progress bar. This progress bar was unintentionally displayed also when using the `--json` option, mixing regular text output with JSON. This is now fixed.

    [#21866](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21866) [#21871](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21871) 

 * Bugfix #21869: Restore old behavior of `snapshots --latest <n>` without `--group-by`

   Restic 0.19.0 accidentally changed the behavior of `snapshots --latest <n>` to no longer group snapshots by host and paths by default.

   The `snapshots --latest <n>` command now again uses the old behavior of grouping by host and paths when `--group-by` is not specified. However, when specifying `--group-by` the output is still grouped as requested, as in restic 0.19.0.

    [#21869](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21869) [#21875](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21875) 

 * Bugfix #21876: Show timezone location in `snapshots` output

   With restic 0.19.0, the `snapshots` command printed the current timezone when listing snapshots. However, that timezone label might change during the year, for example with daylight saving time. Restic now prints a more consistent and shorter version of the text.

    [#21876](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21876) https://forum.restic.net/t/possible-bug-in-timezone-naming/10867

 * Bugfix #21879: Prevent crash in mountpoint validation if mountpoint is inaccessible

   Since restic 0.19.0, the `mount` command validates a mountpoint before loading the repository. If restic was unable to stat the mountpoint, this would result in a crash. This has now been fixed to correctly return an error instead.

    [#21879](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21879) 

 * Bugfix #21895: Remove read-only files via the SFTP backend on Windows servers

   Since restic 0.19.0, repository files on the SFTP backend are marked read-only after save. On Windows SFTP servers, removing them failed with a permission error. The SFTP backend now clears the read-only flag before removing the file.

    [#21895](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21895) [#21897](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21897) 

 * Bugfix #21899: Make `backup` respect excludes for duplicate directory entries

   Since restic 0.19.0, backing up a directory with duplicate directory entries always produced "Warning: at least one source file could not be read", even when those files were excluded. This has now been fixed.

    [#21899](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21899) [#21900](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21900)

frp.changelog:
## Features

* frpc can verify server certificates using system CAs, optionally combined with CAs from `trustedCaFile`.
* `frpc reload` now refreshes certificate files for unchanged `https2http` and `https2https` proxies without interrupting existing connections. Failed refreshes keep the previous certificate and report the error in proxy status and logs while reload still succeeds.
* Added `metricsServer` to both frps and frpc, a separate listener for health checks, metrics and optional profiling that does not expose the dashboard or the admin API. It is disabled unless `metricsServer.port` is set, defaults to `127.0.0.1`, and has its own credentials and TLS. Setting the port serves `/metrics` on both: frps exposes runtime and business metrics, so `enablePrometheus` is not needed there, and frpc exposes Go runtime metrics only, without linking an extra metrics library.

  The `/healthz`, `/metrics` and pprof endpoints on `webServer`, `webServer.pprofEnable` and `enablePrometheus` still work but are deprecated: configure `metricsServer` instead. They will continue to work until v0.80.0 is released, and may be removed in v0.80.0 or later.

## Fixes

* Fixed proxy and visitor configuration changes being lost when reloading frpc during reconnection.
* Updated yamux to fix a 100% CPU busy loop after a session shuts down and a session close that could hang when the underlying connection (for example WebSocket) blocks on a write, which could also delay reconnection.
* frps now closes the multiplexed session of a replaced or failed control connection immediately, releasing its streams and work connections instead of keeping them until keepalive times out.
* Fixed a data race when frpc updates log prefixes while other goroutines are logging, which could crash the process.
* Fixed HTTPS and tcpmux route listeners leaving a pending connection open when the listener is removed during connection handoff; the connection is now closed instead of leaving the client to wait for a read timeout.

aria2-next.changelog:
## Summary

Aria2 Next 3.1.0 changes how failed downloads survive a restart and how redirected downloads are named. A download that failed before the session was saved comes back as failed instead of being started again on every launch. Windows executables now carry version information and an application manifest. Release assets cover the same seven platforms.

### Changed

- Failed downloads are saved to the session with their error code and message and restored as failed results. Previously every launch retried them, so dead links failed again within seconds and produced a burst of errors. Retrying one is still a user action ([rayburst#802](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst/issues/802)).
- Without a Content-Disposition filename or a caller hint, a download that was redirected is named after the URL it landed on, as browsers do. A link such as `…/download/3.28` that redirects to `…/setup.exe` is now saved as `setup.exe` ([rayburst#801](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst/issues/801)).

### Added

- The Windows executable embeds version information and a manifest that declares Windows 10/11 support and long path awareness. Paths beyond `MAX_PATH` work where the system enables long paths ([#86](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/aria2-next/issues/86)).

### Downloads

system-informer.changelog:
# System Informer 4.0

The first 4.0 release: a new kernel/user transport, a Process Monitor, Hybrid Analysis integration, a JSON settings store, a rewritten installer, and a year of fixes across the app, driver, plugins, and phnt headers.

## Highlights

- Process Monitor (Tools menu): a driver-backed live log of process, thread, image, registry, file, handle and silo events with filtering, access-mask decoding, and configurable look-back.
- Hybrid Analysis integration (OnlineChecks): System Informer can now automatically check running processes and loaded images against Hybrid Analysis, showing verdicts directly in the process and module lists via a new Hybrid Analysis column. Unknown files can optionally be submitted for analysis. Results are cached locally so repeated lookups are free, and scanning is opt-in with per-service API keys, path exclusions, and rate handling built in.
- Ring-buffer informer transport in the kernel driver: large shared-memory ring instead of per-message port round-trips, with rate limiting and per-client statistics; informer callbacks run at APC/DPC level where possible.
- New installer: modern wizard with dark mode, DPI scaling, uninstaller, shortcut page, and atomic staged extraction with rollback — failed updates no longer leave a half-written directory.
- Updater: toast-notification flow with progress and actions; BITS, Delivery Optimization and Microsoft Store download back-ends.
- Low-latency mode (experimental, Windows 11): high-resolution provider timers.
- Per-monitor DPI and dark theme work throughout the app, plugins, and property sheets, including Windows 11 borders and much less resize flicker.

## Application

### New
- Users tab (logged-on sessions); process environment editor with multi-entry split editing; WMI tab gains MI support.
- Columns: Short user name, service Username, thread RPC usage, thread kernel stack, handle reference count/size, extended GDI/handle details, ALPC port state; GPU/NPU committed memory.
- Process tree: independent root/child sort options, Collapse/Expand All, aggregate-aware sorting; Ctrl-drag parent fix.
- Threads: Freeze/Thaw, suspended/wait-type highlighting; Modules: native/mapped highlighting and CLR metadata mapping.
- Memory strings search: parallel/bulk scanning, UTF-8, progress, sortable results.
- Services: multi-select start/pause with progress and retry; Run As: per-launch privilege selection and AppContainer launch.
- Handle protect/inherit changes without the driver; COM permission dialogs; desktop heap detection; UDP firewall-exempt port highlighting.
- System Information: reorderable sections, horizontal scrolling, per-CPU speed; overhauled tray mini-info window; energy statistics.
- Options: consolidated Highlighting page, per-tab layout persistence, advanced setting editor; settings.schema.json shipped for editors.
- Hold Shift at startup to launch the original Task Manager when System Informer is the replacement.

### Fixed
- I/O delta columns sorting by cumulative values; page/IO priority in Threads tab; protection column sort; username column not updating.
- Process affinity regressions (single and multi processor groups); main window stealing foreground at startup; previous-instance restore and handle leak.
- Hangs opening the security editor and AFD socket properties; crashes on CPUs without rdtscp, in snapshot handling, on "Current Power Scheme", and with WSL info when no distro is installed.
- Settings not saving on network shares; User Notes not reloaded on restart; Windows 7 import resolution.
- Numerous memory and handle leaks, out-of-bounds reads (CPU info, syscall list, AVX search), and dark-theme painting bugs.

## Kernel driver (KSystemInformer)

- Silo (container) informer; file informer now reports copy operations, access masks and image sizes; thread kernel-stack query; hash-result caching; dedicated system process for driver threads.
- Object protection reworked with broader handle-access stripping and on-demand protection; CID table population optimized; portable mode always unloads the driver on exit.
- Hardening: OBJ_DONT_REPARSE on all internal opens; message/dynamic-data validation and size math hardened; share-check/paging-file open options require MAXIMUM state; "securely created" state requires WinTcb/WinSystem creator; randomized minifilter altitude when load fails; rundown protection for hash/verify.
- Many correctness fixes: native-load race, ring-buffer signaling, informer state leak, file-op buffer/MDL handling, EPROCESS/VPB/pool-tag issues, image-mapping leak, registry post-op strings, thread handle guarantees.

## Security hardening (user mode)

- Updater: the downloaded installer is now re-verified from disk and held with a deny-write handle until launched, failing closed otherwise.
- phsvc: the elevated helper now pins the client image to Systchecks integrity before accepting connections.
- Overflow-checked size math in ACL/security-descriptor, heap and config parsing; DbgHelpVerifyMicrosoftChain setting to verify the dbghelp/symsrv signing chain; remote environment address validation.

## Hybrid Analysis & file reputation (OnlineChecks)

- Automatic reputation scanning of processes and modules with Hybrid Analysis; verdicts surface in a new Hybrid Analysis column and in the file properties.
- Optional automatic submission of unknown files to Hybrid Analysis for sandbox analysis.
- Opt-in setup flow with a Hybrid Analysis partner prompt; perd path exclusions so sensitive directories are never hashed orsubmitted; configurable startup delay.
- Batched hashing and requests with rate-limit handling, and a portable SQLite scan cache shared safely across multiple System Informer processes.

## Plugins

- ExtendedTools: ACPI tables, TPM boot log (WBCL), Power Grid/ and Startup Tasks dialogs; per-adapter/per-node GPU columns and GPU memory mini-info; disk rate columns; better firewall monitor.
- WindowExplorer:

sandboxie-plus.changelog: ![0 5 5](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3890945/105014988-575cb680-5a41-11eb-90d5-d942d28184b2.png) ### Release Notes Sandboxie Plus 1.18.8 / Classic 5.73.8 brings important compatibility improvements for Firefox and other sandboxed browsers, with a particular focus on fixing video playback issues. Video playback now works correctly in sandboxed Firefox on websites such as Disney, Amazon Prime, Netflix, TVNZ and ESPN that rely on mediaCapabilities.decodingInfo() to check media support before starting playback. This resolves an issue that could leave videos unable to start on affected sites. The release also improves AppContainer handling used by browsers and other applications to isolate their child processes. Fixes address missing sandbox permissions and overly restrictive substitute tokens that could prevent these processes from starting or accessing required system resources. Microsoft Edge can again use the corrected substitute token without enabling UnRestrictAppContainerToken by default. A security fix addresses an out-of-bounds read in the GUI proxy’s MapWindowPoints handler that could expose service heap data to sandboxed callers. The Import Boxes workflow has also been corrected, allowing users to choose where imported sandboxes are created. For existing sandboxes, the new fixboxdacls command in KmdUtil.exe adds missing AppContainer access permissions. Advanced configuration options provide additional control: KeepBroadGroupsInAppContainerToken=n restores the previous all-deny-only substitute token behavior, NeutralizeLowBoxToken=n allows direct NtCreateLowBoxToken calls through, and FakeAppContainerToken=n now allows sandboxed programs to create real AppContainer child processes. For a full list of changes please review the [change log](https://github.com/sandboxie-plus/Sandboxie/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#1188--5738---2026-10-17). #### You can support the project through donations, any help will be greatly appreciated. [](https://xanasoft.com/go.php?to=donate) #### If you have issues with an update installation, just uninstall the previous version keeping the sandboxie.ini and reinstall the new build.

zed.changelog:
This week's release includes optional automatic Git fetching, a resizable Refs column in the Git Graph, dragging Git Panel files into terminals and editors, and mouse-wheel font zoom in diff views and terminals.

## Features

### AI

- Added an `edit_predictions.button` setting to toggle the edit prediction button in the status bar. ([#66450](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66450); thanks [z0al](https://github.com/z0al))
- Improved compatibility with the latest Agent Client Protocol, including handling of missing sessions, plan updates, diff formats, and cancellation of permission requests. ([#66425](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66425))
- Improved the Agent's `read_file` tool output by truncating lines longer than 2,000 characters to prevent context window overflow. ([#65395](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/65395); thanks [Antphar](https://github.com/Antphar))
- Improved subagent cards so that full screen opens a finished subagent run at its start. ([#66252](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66252))

### Git

- Added optional automatic fetching of the current branch's upstream remote and the default branch's remote. Enable it with `git.auto_fetch.enabled`; configure the interval with `git.auto_fetch.interval_secs` (60 seconds by default). Automatic fetching is disabled by default. ([#53089](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/53089); thanks [andriygm](https://github.com/andriygm))
- Added a resizable "Refs" column to the Git Graph that can be toggled on or off from the column header's context menu. ([#66260](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66260); thanks [RemcoSmitsDev](https://github.com/RemcoSmitsDev))
- Added support for dragging files from the Git Panel to the terminal and editor panes. ([#66423](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66423); thanks [mmatczuk](https://github.com/mmatczuk))
- Added support for searching by branch name in the worktree picker. ([#66384](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66384); thanks [michelinux](https://github.com/michelinux))

### Debugger

- Added support for configuring the debugger panel’s default size via `debugger.default_width` and `debugger.default_height`. ([#66435](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66435))

### Languages

- Improved call hierarchy readability by adding spacing between item names and details. ([#66144](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66144); thanks [yskim308](https://github.com/yskim308))

### Linux

- Improved window startup time on Linux with NVIDIA GPUs. ([#66002](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66002); thanks [runsonmypc](https://github.com/runsonmypc))

### Other

- Added support for mouse-wheel font zoom in diff views and terminals with `mouse_wheel_zoom` enabled: `cmd-scroll` on macOS and `ctrl-scroll` on Linux/Windows. ([#66296](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66296); thanks [ndri](https://github.com/ndri))
- Improved responsiveness when navigating code, loading completion details, and comparing files. ([#66487](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66487))
- Improved the reliability of language server and agent downloads with consistent checksum verification, rejection of failed HTTP responses, and better cleanup of partial downloads. ([#66048](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66048))

## Bug Fixes

- Fixed a bug where launching Zed on Windows while it was already running prevented the previous session from being restored. ([#66364](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66364); thanks [somtri](https://github.com/somtri))
- Fixed Agent context compaction unnecessarily using uncached input tokens with supported providers, including OpenAI and xAI. ([#64938](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/64938); thanks [tidely](https://github.com/tidely))
- Fixed auto-compaction only running once during a long agent turn, which could let the thread exceed the model's context window. ([#66215](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66215))
- Fixed compaction not reusing the prompt cache for ChatGPT subscription models. ([#66527](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66527))
- Fixed creating pull requests from Zed for Forgejo remotes, including Codeberg. ([#66182](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66182); thanks [Lachstec](https://github.com/Lachstec))
- Fixed external agents sometimes starting without MCP servers configured in user settings when the thread was created before the project folder finished loading. ([#64612](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/64612); thanks [philwinder](https://github.com/philwinder))
- Fixed Helix mode operations overwriting the system clipboard when `vim.use_system_clipboard` was set to `"always"`. ([#55455](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/55455); thanks [SrGaabriel](https://github.com/SrGaabriel))
- Fixed local files opening as empty buffers in remote workspaces. ([#65771](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/65771); thanks [Huliiiiii](https://github.com/Huliiiiii))
- Fixed mentioning, sharing, and deleting project skills in remote workspaces. ([#66207](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66207))
- Fixed Project Search buttons affecting the wrong pane when clicked in an unfocused split. ([#50882](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/50882); thanks [transitoryangel](https://github.com/transitoryangel))
- Fixed registry agents installed via npm (such as Claude Agent) failing to launch with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` after an interrupted or concurrent install. ([#66235](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66235))
- Fixed remote terminals and tasks failing on Windows SSH servers whose default shell is Nushell. ([#65580](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/65580); thanks [lingyaochu](https://github.com/lingyaochu))
- Fixed remote workspaces sharing a directory being merged into one workspace after restarting Zed. ([#66289](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66289); thanks [buvidk1234](http

escrcpy.changelog:
# 🚀 Escrcpy 3.3.1 — Unlock Existing Features, Embrace a New Chapter

Escrcpy 3.3.1 is a **transitional release** that bridges the gap between the existing version and the new billing and licensing system planned for Escrcpy 4.0.0 and later.

To ensure a smooth transition, **all existing features in Escrcpy 3.3.1 are available for free**, with no purchase, activation, or license verification required. This is a long-term policy for the existing version, not a limited-time promotion.

This release also improves the stability of embedded mirroring and application startup workflows.

## ✨ What's New

### 🔓 All Existing Features Unlocked

Due to adjustments to our billing platform and subscription system, all existing features in Escrcpy 3.3.1 are now available for free.

This policy is intended to help existing users transition smoothly to the new version strategy. You can continue using all features available in Escrcpy 3.3.1 without additional payment.

### 🖥️ Embedded Mirroring & Virtual Displays

- Introduced preliminary support for launching applications on virtual displays and using embedded mirroring.
- Improved the stability of application startup logic related to embedded mirrored virtual screens.
- Fixed abnormal mirroring control parameters when launching applications through shortcuts.
- Fixed an application launch issue affecting some Windows users.

### 🤖 Copilot Configuration

Copilot now requires users to configure a supported AI model provider, including the relevant API key, endpoint, and model settings.

If no provider is configured, the interface prompts users to complete the setup instead of automatically using the previous built-in service.

Please note that third-party AI model providers may charge for API usage according to their own pricing policies.

## ⚠️ Important Upgrade Notice

Due to adjustments to the billing and subscription system, users running Escrcpy 3.2.0 or earlier may encounter license verification issues or find that certain features no longer work correctly.

**We recommend upgrading to Escrcpy 3.3.1 as soon as possible.** All existing features in this release are unlocked and can be used without additional payment.

## 🔮 Looking Ahead: Escrcpy 4.0.0+

Escrcpy 4.0.0 and later versions are planned to introduce a new billing and licensing system, along with new features and services.

- **A new licensing system:** Future versions will use a separate licensing and purchasing system.
- **Launch promotion:** A three-day introductory promotion with special pricing is planned. Pricing and details will be announced separately.
- **Your existing version remains available:** You can continue using Escrcpy 3.3.1 and all its unlocked features without purchasing a newer version.
- **Previous purchases will not automatically transfer:** Purchases made under the previous system will not automatically grant paid entitlements under the new system.

Escrcpy 3.3.1 serves as a bridge between the existing version and the upcoming licensing system. You can continue using the current version or consider upgrading when the new version becomes available.

## 🙏 Thank You

Thank you for your continued support and feedback. We hope Escrcpy 3.3.1 provides a more stable experience and helps make this transition smooth as we prepare for the next chapter of Escrcpy.

stability-matrix.changelog:
> Full technical notes for this release: [docs.lykos.ai/stability-matrix/release-notes/2.16.5](https://docs.lykos.ai/stability-matrix/release-notes/2.16.5)
## Added
- Added **Fizgig**, a LoRA training studio for Flux 2 Klein 9B, Krea 2, MiniMax H3 and Qwen Image 2.1 with dataset prep, training, LoRA repair and extraction in one app ([#1761](https://github.com/LykosAI/StabilityMatrix/pull/1761)) - thanks to @e-nord!
- Added AMD ROCm support for **Stable Diffusion WebUI Forge - Neo** on Windows and Linux. Forge Neo's developer supports NVIDIA only, so report AMD issues with it to Stability Matrix ([#1770](https://github.com/LykosAI/StabilityMatrix/pull/1770)) - thanks to @NeuralFault!

## Changed
- ComfyUI now installs and updates from its current GitHub home, [Comfy-Org/ComfyUI](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI)

## Fixed
- Fixed **Wan2GP** installs on Python 3.11 failing with `sageattention ... has no wheels with a matching Python version tag`. New Wan2GP installs now use Python 3.11 with PyTorch 2.10 and CUDA 13 with matching Triton, SageAttention and Flash Attention, the same setup Wan2GP's own installer uses. CUDA 13 needs NVIDIA driver 580 or newer. GTX 10XX cards stay on Python 3.10
- Existing **Wan2GP** installs on Python 3.10 keep their PyTorch 2.7 setup when updated. If a newer model such as LTX 2.5 fails with a Triton error, add Wan2GP again as a new install, which now uses Python 3.11, and move your outputs across ([#1756](https://github.com/LykosAI/StabilityMatrix/issues/1756))
- Fixed ComfyUI updates downgrading SageAttention post6 to post4 and reinstalling compatible wheels ([#1764](https://github.com/LykosAI/StabilityMatrix/issues/1764)).
- Fixed ComfyUI installation and updates failing on Python 3.13+ because the NumPy 1.x constraint has no compatible wheel ([#1754](https://github.com/LykosAI/StabilityMatrix/issues/1754))
- Fixed **AI-Toolkit** installation failing on Linux while unpacking Node.js with a "Dangerous link path" error ([#1767](https://github.com/LykosAI/StabilityMatrix/issues/1767))
- Fixed **Windows ROCm** PyTorch installs pairing mismatched `torch` and `torchvision` versions, which broke packages at `import torchvision` ([#1769](https://github.com/LykosAI/StabilityMatrix/pull/1769)) - thanks to @NeuralFault!
- ControlNet preprocessing in Inference now offers to update older tagged Inference Core Nodes installs to a version with the ControlNet import fixes and Python 3.12/3.13 support
- Fixed the package uninstall confirmation counting your whole shared model library for packages using symlink sharing. Only the package's own files are counted; shared models were never deleted
- Fixed logs ignoring `--home-dir`, and opening a missing folder or file showing an error dialog instead of a short notice ([#1766](https://github.com/LykosAI/StabilityMatrix/pull/1766)) - thanks to @e-nord!
- Fixed shared model folder links hiding **DiffusionModels** in the Checkpoint Manager, Image Lab and Inference, including when DiffusionModels is itself a link ([#1743](https://github.com/LykosAI/StabilityMatrix/pull/1743), [#1763](https://github.com/LykosAI/StabilityMatrix/pull/1763)) - thanks to @NeuralFault and @ionite34!
- Fixed the Model Browser's **Base Model** filter being lost when using **Next Model** / **Previous Model** or refreshing a model's details ([#1436](https://github.com/LykosAI/StabilityMatrix/issues/1436))
- Fixed **Open on CivArchive** opening a file URL instead of the model page on Linux ([#1765](https://github.com/LykosAI/StabilityMatrix/issues/1765))
- Fixed emoji showing as `��` in Image Lab messages and in CivitAI and CivArchive model descriptions
- Fixed release-note text being cut off beside the scrollbar in the update dialog ([#1757](https://github.com/LykosAI/StabilityMatrix/issues/1757))
- Fixed text in **Image Lab** messages and thinking blocks being cut off at the right edge. Message bubbles now fit their text, and inline code is easier to read
- Fixed **Save & Regenerate** in Image Lab deleting later images and dropping the edited message's attachments. It now shows progress and can be cancelled
- Fixed **Regenerate** in Image Lab removing the old response before the new one was ready. A failed or cancelled regenerate now keeps it
- Fixed Image Lab pulling you back to a conversation when its generation finished while you were in another, and showing that generation's error in the one you had open
- Fixed deleting one image from a multi-image message in Image Lab deleting your original file when Image Lab hadn't kept its own copy
- Fixed your message in Image Lab not being editable or deletable after a failed or cancelled generation
- Fixed cancelling a Gemini generation in Image Lab showing "Generation failed" instead of "Cancelled"
- Fixed Image Lab not scrolling to a new message when you were already at the bottom of the conversation
- Fixed a ComfyUI generation in Image Lab not stopping when ComfyUI disconnected, if you had opened a Gemini conversation in the meantime
- Fixed package version lists and update checks showing an old release as the newest, because startup update checks ran into GitHub's rate limit

## Supporters
### 🌟 Visionaries
This patch is a good one for AMD owners: Forge Neo now runs on ROCm on both Windows and Linux, and Windows ROCm installs always get a `torch` and `torchvision` that actually match. It also adds Fizgig, a whole LoRA training studio, to the package list. readest.changelog:
## Release Highlights
* Vocabulary: You can now build a vocabulary list, mark words as Learning or Mastered for Word Lens hints, and sync with Anki
* Statistics: Added a reading statistics dashboard so you can see your reading habits at a glance
* Reading: Added Page Flip and paper curl page turns, a page preview while dragging the progress slider, a straight-line reading ruler, and keyboard-only text selection
* Styling: You can now ignore publisher fonts, make white image backgrounds transparent, and adjust dialogue highlighting
* Text-to-Speech: You can now preview voices, pick a default voice per language, and sync downloaded read-aloud audio across devices
* Library: You can now import pasted text and Word or RTF files, share collections as bundles, search for covers in the app
* Sync: Added Grimmory, Obsidian, and CrossPoint 2.0 highlight sync, a new view of where your reading data goes, and a switch for servers with self-signed certificates
* Dictionary: You can now resize the dictionary popup, customize AI context lookups, edit word hints, and choose your lookup app on Android
* PDF: Text is now sharper, especially on iOS and Android, with smoother pinch zoom, panning, and gapless horizontal scrolling
* More: The KOReader plugin can sign in with a QR code, iPhone Duo gets book mode on its inner display, and stylus annotation and sync are more reliable

appflowy.changelog:
### 🚀 v0.15.0

#### New Features

- **Dashboards** — Added dashboards combining views from multiple databases, with movable and resizable widgets, shared filters, and personal filter changes. Local dashboards could reuse existing views; creating new widget views required a server connection.
- **Charts and drill-downs** — Added Number charts for workspaces with Pro features, expanded grouping and display controls, and drill-down tables for exploring a chart's records and saving the result as a filtered view.
- **Page widths** — Added full-width and custom-width formatting per document, shared with collaborators while retaining each user's default for pages without an explicit width.
- **Image search results** — Showed the image and matched text behind a search result, and opened documents at the matched image when the server supplied this information.
- **Native update installation** — Added user-initiated installation on macOS and Windows x64 when the server enabled it and supplied a signed update feed. Retained manual downloads when native installation was unavailable.

#### Improvements

- **Database exports** — Added A4, A3, Letter, and Legal paper sizes with portrait or landscape orientation. Paginated wide PDF tables at a readable size and exported the active view's visible fields and current rows, with support for complete offline caches.
- **Board views** — Added sorting within columns, column calculations, and backgrounds based on group colors.
- **Images** — Saved thumbnails and decoded images at their display size across documents and database cards, reducing the size of images held in memory.
- **Translations** — Updated interface translations and corrected Grid header and cell alignment in right-to-left languages.

#### Bug Fixes

- Preserved individual heading text during multi-block conversion, kept link formatting when editing URLs, and allowed read-only toggle blocks to expand without changing the shared document.
- Prevented moving subpages in the sidebar from sending them to Trash, and preserved external-link and date mentions when copying or exporting document text.
- Corrected row peek navigation and calendar row opening, focused newly added Grid rows for editing, and kept hidden Board groups usable during partial schema refreshes.
- Preserved document image sizes while scrolling and recovered missing or damaged media caches without losing image authentication.
- Prevented duplicated database content from uploading before its page was acknowledged by the server, and preserved database layouts when reopening views.
- Fixed PDF image reading with Ollama models that advertised vision support through their capabilities.

#### ⚠️ Action Required

- Self-hosted workspaces still require **AppFlowy Cloud v0.19.10 or later**.
- Self-hosted dashboards require server support for the Dashboard layout. Before using more than twelve widgets or four widgets in one row, deploy the updated dashboard validation to every realtime server.

## What's Changed

**⚠️ This update contains important security fixes. Please upgrade as soon as possible**.

- Shared decks could execute arbitrary code via iframes when viewed in the editor ([GHSA-j9v5-m549-cg6c](https://github.com/ankitects/anki/security/advisories/GHSA-j9v5-m549-cg6c)). Thanks to @DePierre for the report.
- On macOS, shared decks could execute arbitrary commands via specially crafted image filenames when the "Show in Folder" editor action is used ([GHSA-gfvm-4968-jp9m](https://github.com/ankitects/anki/security/advisories/GHSA-gfvm-4968-jp9m)). Thanks to @hyperreality and @Hama1cco for the reports.
- Compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates are now disallowed. This is in response to a [widespread security incident](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/) affecting most systems and web browsers. **Updating Anki might not be enough. Please make sure your system is fully up to date.**

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ankitects/anki/compare/26.09.3...26.09.4

zettlr.changelog:
**Quality of Life Improvements | Cleanup | Fixes**

This new update of Zettlr primarily fixes things that were either broken for some time, or broke in 4.9. However, it also includes a set of features and other improvements that will come in handy.

Among the most notable changes in this update are: (1) attachments specified in BibTeX or BibLaTeX libraries are properly opened via the context menu in Zettlr; (2) Mermaid diagrams will render again; (3) keywords and tags in YAML frontmatters are clickable again; (4) we fixed a bunch of shortcuts that stopped working after the custom shortcut update; (5) the LanguageTool linter now additionally checks various text-fields in your frontmatters; and (6) we have begun homogenizing Zettlr's UI across all platforms. macOS-users should not see many differences, but on Windows and Linux, the app will look considerably different. This change does not affect the placement or functionality of any UI elements, only their styling.

There's much more that has changed, so we again invite you to read the Changelog below before updating. Happy writing!

> **Do you enjoy Zettlr? Then consider making a donation to help us pay for the development costs. You can donate [monthly on Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/zettlr) or [once via PayPal](https://www.paypal.me/hendrikerz). Additionally, you can directly [sponsor Hendrik Erz on GitHub](https://github.com/sponsors/nathanlesage) or [send a tip on Ko-Fi](https://ko-fi.com/hendrikerz). Thanks for your support!**

# Changelog

## GUI and Functionality

- **Feature**: The context menus for links and images now also feature various
  items that may be useful for formatting aspects of the link/image descriptions
  (#6417).
- **Feature**: Make the "find next" and "find previous" commands of the editor
  search configurable. Previously, both `Mod-g` and `F3` would move to the next
  search result, but after implementing custom shortcuts, these two commands
  were left unconfigurable and hard-coded to `Mod-g`. These are now configurable
  so that you can change the default keybinding of `Mod-g` to `F3` if you wish
  (#6575).
- **Feature**: The LanguageTool linter now also lints text-only properties in
  the frontmatter, using the same language as the rest of the document. This
  allows spotting issues with these metadata fields as well. Currently, the
  linter includes in its detection the following properties:
    - `title`
    - `subtitle`
    - `abstract`
    - `abstract-title`
    - `description`
    - `shorttitle`
    - `shortsubtitle`
    - `thanks`
- **Change**: The styles and layouts of various UI components have been
  adjusted. The following components should now look mostly the same across all
  operating systems:
    - Toolbar
    - File Tree
    - Sidebar
- **Change**: Removed the `.md` extension from the default new filename pattern
  in the Advanced Preferences menu. This pattern is used as the filename, so the
  extension is unnecessary. Previously, creating a new file with the default
  pattern would result in the `.md` extension being added twice to markdown
  files, or added incorrectly to non-markdown files. Existing users should
  update the pattern manually by removing `.md` from it. For new installations,
  the pattern will be correct. (#6638).
- **Change**: The layout of the document information popover is now improved.
  We have moved the bold styling over to the actually important parts, improved
  legibility of the popover, and included more information -- notably,
  regardless of which unit (words or characters) you select in the preferences,
  the popover will now display both numbers, with your preferred one clearly
  visible.
- Fixed a misaligned size distribution between the file manager, editor view,
  and sidebar. Now, when double-clicking the dividers between these three
  components, they will resize so that both sidebars take up 20% of the window
  width, as opposed to a distribution of 20% for the file manager and ca. 15%
  for the sidebar. This way, both sidebars of the main window are visually
  equally sized.
- Fixed a bug where Zettlr would *never* load attachments from your main
  database if that database was in `BibTeX` or `BibLaTeX` format, as a small
  logical error made the relevant code for retrieving attachments never find the
  database in memory and thus would always fall back to attempting to contact
  Zotero, which would, logically, fail for JabRef users (#6619).
- Library loading on boot is now asynchronous, also we register a
  long-running task during database loads to visualize especially the loading of
  large library files.
- Fixed a bug that prevented Mermaid diagrams from rendering due to an
  underlying bug in the new API (#6625).
- Fixed an issue that would cause full-text searches to start even as the input
  field was still composing non-latin text (#6597; #6604).
- Fixed the spacing on the changelog entries to make it more pleasant to read.
- Fixed an issue that could, under the right circumstances, write unusual values
  for resized split views into the configuration, necessitating a configuration
  modification to render Zettlr usable again (#5829).
- Fixes various issues pertaining to keywords/tags which are present in YAML
  frontmatters of files. Zettlr now again correctly detects these and they are
  clickable, yielding a search for keywords, which also includes keywords with
  spaces (#2443; #2590; #4498; see PR #6496).
- Fixed a 404-link to an old documentation page in the onboarding dialog.
- Fixed the LanguageTool language overrides. Previously, if you wanted to change
  the language in which LanguageTool would check your document via the `lang`
  property (e.g., `lang: fr` to force French instead of autodetection), you had
  to reload the entire document. Now changes are detected on the fly as you
  modify the `lang` property in the YAML frontmatter.

FreeCAD 1.1.4 is the last planned maintenance release in the 1.1.x series. It includes two security fixes addressing file-handling vulnerabilities that can be triggered by opening a maliciously crafted FCStd file. All previously-released versions are affected by these issues, so we strongly recommend that all users upgrade, especially anyone who opens FreeCAD files from untrusted or unknown sources.

Highlights & Features:
===
- **Updated builds:** a small maintenance release rebuilt on new runners with updated FFmpeg dependencies and stronger packaging checks.
- **GPU exports:** added AMD AMF and HEVC NVENC/QSV presets, sharper GPU badges on high-DPI displays, and validated GPU alternatives before falling back to CPU encoding. Export targets and badges now follow the actual encoder.

floorp.changelog:
## Floorp の今後の開発方針について

いつも Floorp をご利用いただき、ありがとうございます。

最近、Floorp のアップデート後の不具合や、既存機能との競合が複数報告されています。問題の報告や調査にご協力いただいている皆さまに、心より感謝申し上げます。

Firefox の標準リリース周期は 2 週間に短縮され、Floorp もこれまで以上に頻繁に Firefox の変更に対応する必要があります。Floorp は Firefox をベースに多数の独自機能を提供しているため、Firefox 本体の変更と独自機能の組み合わせで予期しない不具合が起こることがあります。 [Mozilla のリリース周期に関する案内](https://blog.mozilla.org/sumo/2026/08/19/firefox-new-release-cadence-and-what-to-expect/)

**今後数か月間、Floorp は新機能の開発・追加を原則として一時停止し、既存機能の修正と安定性の向上に開発リソースを集中します。**

この期間は、以下の改善を優先します。

- 既知の不具合やクラッシュの修正
- Firefox の更新に伴う互換性問題への対応
- タブ、ワークスペース、サイドバーなどの既存機能の安定化
- 自動テストと回帰テストの強化
- 問題のある機能を安全に無効化できる仕組みの検討

セキュリティアップデートや必要な修正パッチは、この期間も引き続き提供します。

Floorp を毎日安心して使っていただけるよう、まずは既存の機能が確実に動作することを優先します。新機能を楽しみにしてくださっている皆さまにはお待ちいただくことになりますが、Floorp の開発は今後も続けていきます。引き続き、ご理解とご協力をよろしくお願いいたします。

Floorp Projects

## Floorp’s development priorities for the coming months

Thank you for using Floorp.

We’ve recently received several reports of bugs after Floorp updates and of conflicts affecting existing features. We’re grateful to everyone who has reported issues and helped us investigate them.

Firefox has moved to a standard two-week release cycle, so Floorp needs to adapt to Firefox changes more frequently. Floorp builds on Firefox with many features of its own, and changes in Firefox can interact with those features in unexpected ways. [Mozilla’s announcement about the Firefox release cycle](https://blog.mozilla.org/sumo/2026/08/19/firefox-new-release-cadence-and-what-to-expect/)

**For the next few months, we’ll generally pause development and rollout of new Floorp features and focus on fixing and improving the stability of existing features.**

During this period, we’ll prioritize the following work.

- Fixing known bugs and crashes
- Addressing compatibility issues introduced by Firefox updates
- Improving the stability of existing features such as tabs, workspaces, and the sidebar
- Strengthening automated tests and regression coverage
- Exploring ways to safely disable features that are causing problems

We’ll continue to provide security updates and necessary bug fixes throughout this period.

We want Floorp to be a browser you can rely on every day. If you’ve been looking forward to new features, thank you for your patience while we focus on making the features you already use work reliably. We’ll continue developing Floorp and appreciate your understanding and support.

Floorp Projects

[日本語リリースノート](https://blog.floorp.app/ja/release/12.21.2/) · [English release notes](https://blog.floorp.app/en/release/12.21.2/)

zen-browser.changelog:
# Zen Stable Release


## Security
- https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-125/

## New Features
- Updated to Firefox 160.0
- Added pause context menu button for the downloads section
- The urlbar now has a bit of transparency for a more modern look.
- The Picture-in-Picture player now has a playback speed setting, with options ranging from 0.25x to 2.0x speed. The setting appears only when the player window is medium-sized or larger.
- Pages saved as PDF now make mathematical content (MathML) accessible to assistive technology such as screen readers.
- Websites that repeatedly ask to handle email (mailto:) and other links can now be blocked with a new “Never allow” button, and blocked sites can be managed in Settings.
- Zen now plays Matroska (MKV) files with FLAC, MP3, or PCM audio.
- WebGL content on macOS is now rendered using Apple's Metal graphics API, which can improve performance on some sites.

## Fixes
- Improved performance for boosts color tinting.
- Fixed the first character typed into the address bar or search bar sometimes being lost when typing quickly right after clicking into it.
- Fixed Zen freezing for several seconds when signing in to intranet sites that use NTLM or Kerberos (Negotiate) authentication.
- Fixed double-tapping or long-pressing a word to select it, and tapping to place the cursor, not working near the cursor in text fields.
- Fixed links opened in the background from other apps on macOS, such as RSS readers, bringing Zen to the foreground.
- Fixed downloaded files on macOS sometimes opening in the wrong application instead of the default one set in Finder.
- Fixed simultaneous downloads on macOS never finishing when Zen is set to ask where to save files. Only the first file showed a save dialog.
- Restored meaningful filenames and the usual save workflow for PDFs opened in Preview from the macOS print dialog.
- More bug fixes and improvements.

## Changes
- The address bar context menu now shows "Paste and Search" instead of "Paste and Go" when the copied text is a search term rather than a web address.

# 2.0.4

## 新功能

- 新增简易模式，可视化编辑订阅、代理组、规则、规则集、DNS 及域名嗅探配置
- 简易模式支持本地节点管理、节点链接导入及订阅代理集合高级设置
- 支持从连接详情快速添加简易模式规则，内联规则集支持列表编辑
- 新增切换节点时仅关闭当前代理组连接的选项
- 新增 DNS 覆写保护开关、日志等级筛选及 macOS 流量文字颜色设置
- 侧边栏折叠后支持悬停展开

## 性能优化

- 优化历史流量统计迁移，减少磁盘写入并增加迁移提示
- 优化跨平台连接应用识别及图标处理，改进 Linux 应用图标匹配

## 修复

- 修复系统唤醒后 TUN 重建时配置不完整，以及修改 TUN 设置后未重启内核的问题
- 修复启动时未等待初始代理集合就绪及代理组选择状态未刷新的问题
- 修复不含节点的远程订阅模板无法使用，以及订阅自动更新间隔字段不一致的问题
- 修复配置模式切换同步、代理组编辑模式及首次使用引导的本地化问题
- 修复 Windows 7 窗口初始化兼容问题，切换系统标题栏时增加重启确认
- 修复拓扑图平移与卡片排序冲突、DNS 卡片切换时尺寸变化的问题
- 修复 YAML 编辑器最大化后尺寸未更新、窄页面标题换行及内核版本名称过长的问题
- 修复代理显示设置菜单选择后自动关闭、Smart 内核设置分隔线及内核认证提示问题

## 其他

ankidroid.changelog:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> GitHub does not auto-update apps


## For regular users

Install `arm64-v8a` from the **Assets** section below. If it fails to install, use `Parallel.A`.

`Parallel` builds install side-by-side with the main APK, allowing you to use different settings and profiles (via the `AnkiDroid directory` advanced setting and a different AnkiWeb login).


## For testers

The builds with `full`, `play` and `amazon` are useful for testing our builds for different app stores:

- **`full`**: F-Droid & GitHub `Parallel` apks
- **`play`**: Google Play - does not have `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` permission as it is forbidden by Google, on uninstall the user is invited to delete data.
- **`amazon`**: Amazon - currently same as full, historically removed `CAMERA` permission


## ABI variants

We perform ABI splits to reduce APK size. In rare cases, a phone may not be using the `arm64-v8a` ABI. You can find your phone's ABI using [kamgurgul/cpu-info](https://github.com/kamgurgul/cpu-info). If disk space isn't an issue, use the `full` apk.

clash-nyanpasu.changelog:
> 简体中文版本请展开页面底部的「简体中文」。 ## Read Before Upgrading - **With TUN on, the TUN stack chosen in Clash settings now takes precedence over a Profile's `tun.stack`.** Previously a stack written by the subscription won. If you relied on it, choose the stack in settings instead (the default is gVisor). - **A Profile that sets a TUN stack the selected core rejects now fails to apply, with an error naming the value and the supported ones.** For example, `tun.stack: mixed` or `mips` under Clash Premium, which would otherwise make the core reject the whole config. This is checked even while TUN is off, because the core parses the key on load. Values Nyanpasu does not know are still passed to the core. - **The stack selector only lists the stacks the current core reads**, and is hidden for clash-rs and Meow, which ignore the key. If the saved stack is not supported by the core you switch to, gVisor is used and a warning is written to the log; the saved setting is kept. - **Service mode now requires nyanpasu-service 2.0.2.** An installed 2.0.1 service is upgraded once at startup. 2.0.2 fixes a stale pid record that made the service and the app fail on every start (#6033). ## Highlights - **Mips (Mihomo IP Stack)**, mihomo's new user-space TUN stack, can be selected under mihomo and mihomo-alpha, together with its TCP congestion controller (CUBIC, Reno, BBR, BBRv3, or the core default). The controller is remembered when you switch to another stack and back (#6091). - **Startup failures no longer crash the app.** A dialog names the file, the cause and the recovery steps, and can open the containing, backup or log folder. 简体中文 ## 升级前须知 - **开启 TUN 时，Clash 设置中选择的 TUN 堆栈现在优先于 Profile 中的 `tun.stack`。** 以前订阅写入的堆栈会覆盖设置。如果你依赖订阅指定堆栈，请改在设置中选择（默认为 gVisor）。 - **Profile 设置了当前内核不支持的 TUN 堆栈时，配置现在会生成失败，错误信息会列出该值与内核支持的值。** 例如在 Clash Premium 下写 `tun.stack: mixed` 或 `mips`，否则内核会拒绝加载整份配置。由于内核加载配置时就会解析这个键，TUN 关闭时也会检查。Nyanpasu 不认识的值仍会原样交给内核。 - **堆栈选择器只列出当前内核会读取的堆栈**，clash-rs 与 Meow 不读取该键，因此不再显示选择器。如果保存的堆栈不被切换后的内核支持，运行时改用 gVisor 并在日志中记录警告，保存的设置不变。 - **服务模式现在需要 nyanpasu-service 2.0.2。** 已安装的 2.0.1 服务会在启动时自动升级一次。2.0.2 修复了残留的 pid 记录导致服务与应用每次启动都失败的问题（#6033）。 ## 主要变更 - **Mips（Mihomo IP Stack）**：mihomo 新增的用户态 TUN 堆栈，可在 mihomo 与 mihomo-alpha 下选择，并可设置 TCP 拥塞控制算法（CUBIC、Reno、BBR、BBRv3 或内核默认）。切换到其他堆栈再切回时，该设置会保留（#6091）。 - **启动失败不再导致应用崩溃。** 对话框会说明出错的文件、原因与恢复步骤，并可打开所在目录、备份目录或日志目录。损坏的本地数据与不可用的任务日志会被重建，不再阻止启动。 - 修复了 Logo 动画边缘、滚动时页面标题与流量迷你图拉伸的显示问题；更新链接与顶部菜单对齐。 - Windows 安装包随 enableLoopback 附带 Windows App SDK 引导程序。 完整的变更列表见上方英文部分。
